issues.description: Function 'config_system': the problem statement (problem_statement.md) requires implementing config_system that accepts a pointer to a Config struct (line 22). The solution implementation (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm) defines a label 'config_system:' that treats the stack parameter as an integer (comment: "logic expecting integer in [esp+4]") and reads [esp+4] into eax directly (line 6). The template (template_repository/helloWorld.asm) does not provide a config_system stub for students to implement, so students following the problem text will implement pointer-based logic but the provided reference implementation expects a plain integer. This mismatch (expected parameter semantics: pointer vs integer) will prevent straightforward verification against the reference and will confuse students about the correct parameter type and calling convention to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make parameter semantics consistent across artifacts and provide a clear student stub. Either (A) update the solution's config_system to accept a pointer: read the pointer from [esp+4], dereference the Config fields as required, and adjust the comment to reflect pointer handling; or (B) if the intended parameter is an integer, update the problem statement to state that config_system expects an integer value. Additionally, add a config_system stub with the chosen signature and a short comment to template_repository/helloWorld.asm so students know where and how to implement it.
